author: Indy Standard
title: Johnson County lawmakers say local schools recognized for literacy achievements
text:
Local schools in Johnson County were recently recognized for high literacy rates by the Indiana Department of Education, according to a statement from county legislators on April 15.
The recognition highlights the work of educators and students in achieving strong reading skills, which lawmakers say is essential for academic success and future opportunities.
More than 400 schools statewide received recognition at the Literacy Achievement Celebration at the Statehouse on April 8 for achieving a 95% or higher passage rate on the 2025 Indiana Reading Evaluation and Determination (IREAD) assessment. “This is a remarkable achievement, showcasing the dedication of teachers across our community,” said State Representative Rob Greene. “Through their efforts, our students have a strong foundation to propel them into the future.”
State Representative Craig Haggard said, “Literacy is where communication and problem-solving begin for Hoosier kids. Our schools are building the next generation of leaders and a stronger Indiana.” The list of recognized area schools was included in the announcement.
State Representative Michelle Davis congratulated local schools and emphasized that strong literacy forms “the foundation of a student’s education” while ensuring that children are set up for success. Davis also co-authored House Enrolled Act 1558 in 2023 to implement science-based reading standards and provide targeted support to students facing reading challenges. According to legislators, last year’s third grade reading scores improved by nearly five percentage points—the largest single-year increase since IREAD began in 2013—bringing proficiency levels back to pre-pandemic rates with more than 87% demonstrating proficiency.
These results come after Indiana placed sixth nationally for fourth- and eighth-grade reading scores in the most recent National Assessment of Education Progress rankings. State Representative Peggy Mayfield said, “Educators and parents in Johnson County are working together to make sure our students succeed. These results are a testament to the success of their partnership and the incredible dedication and effort occurring in our schools.”
Results from individual schools’ IREAD assessments can be found on IDOE’s website.
